 Jalen Suggs, Jase Richardson, Desmond Bane, Franz Wagner and Wendell Carter Jr. will start Sunday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Sunday’s game is Orlando’s first since losing Paolo Banchero to a low-grade right ankle sprain during Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves. The Magic will go small on Sunday, with Richardson’s inclusion in the lineup meaning that Bane and Wagner will shift down a position. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Magic head coach Sean Sweeney said that the team is leaning toward starting Jase Richardson in Sunday’s game against the Knicks. 
 A final decision has not been made, but Richardson could be the addition to the starting lineup after Orlando lost Paolo Banchero (ankle) during Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves. If he starts, Desmond Bane and Franz Wagner would shift to small forward and power forward, respectively. 
 Jase Richardson 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Jase Richardson (back) is not on the injury report ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Richardson exited early from Friday’s preseason game with a back injury, but that won’t keep him from suiting up in the season opener. Anthony Black (ankle) has been ruled out, so Richardson may take on a few extra minutes off the bench in the backcourt. 
 Jase Richardson 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Jase Richardson (back) will not return to Friday’s exhibition against the Heat. 
 Richardson played seven minutes in the first half of Friday’s preseason finale before being shut down with a sore lower back. Orlando has a few days before its regular-season opener; hopefully, that’s enough time for the second-year guard to return to full strength. With Anthony Black still recovering from a sprained ankle, Richardson may get to play a few more minutes early in the season. 
 Jase Richardson 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Jase Richardson accounted for 12 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and one steal in Sunday’s exhibition against the Cavaliers. 
 Orlando did not play Jalen Suggs or Anthony Black on Sunday, so Richardson started. After a rookie season averaging just 10.9 minutes per game, Richardson’s outlook in redraft leagues isn’t particularly good, especially with Suggs and Black healthy. However, he’s still worth rostering in dynasty leagues. 
 Jase Richardson 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Jace Richardson accounted for 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, six assists and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Heat. 
 After a solid 15-point effort in his first action of the summer on Thursday, Richardson was even better on Saturday. In addition to shooting the ball well on all three levels, he did not commit a turnover and led the Magic in assists. Richardson didn’t get to play much last season, and a good run in Las Vegas is the first step toward ensuring that he’s in Orlando’s plans for 2026-27. At this rate, the Magic may decide that they’ve seen enough from the guard to shut him down for the remainder of summer league. 
 Jase Richardson 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Jase Richardson contributed 15 points (6-of-14 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Hornets on Thursday. 
 Richardson didn’t play a ton as a rookie, but he’s an incredibly talented player. He should see his role increase in year two, though it likely won’t be large enough for him to hold any fantasy relevance. He was productive during his two summer league performances last year as well, and he may not see many more appearances in Las Vegas.

 Jalen Suggs (knee) was helped back to the Magic locker room during the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Suggs was driving to the basket for an uncontested layup when his right knee hyperextended. The Magic guard remained down on the court for a few minutes before being helped back to the locker room. Suggs could put some weight on his right leg, but the injury could keep him out for a while. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Williams exited late in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game against the Clippers after suffering a serious left leg injury. 
 Williams suffered a serious left leg injury late in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game, with team doctors applying an air cast before taking him off the court on a stretcher. He’ll miss an unknown amount of time, but the Thunder forward is likely looking at a lengthy absence. Jared McCain replaced Williams in the Thunder lineup.

 Egor Dëmin recorded three points (1-of-6 FGs), one assist, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Pacers.
 Coming off of a 22-point effort in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers, Dëmin shot 1-of-6 from the field on Sunday. He’s been inconsistent thus far, with the stellar showing against Cleveland sandwiched between poor efforts against the Horners and Pacers. In those two contests, Dëmin shot a combined 3-of-16 from the field and recorded four assists and five turnovers. He’ll look to bounce back on Tuesday against the Celtics. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Julius Randle finished Sunday’s loss to the Pacers with 10 points (2-of-8 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists and one steal.
 Randle shot poorly on Sunday, but he posted solid rebounding and assist numbers. Technically speaking, Egor Dëmin is the Nets’ starting point guard. However, Randle has facilitated a lot in the team’s first three games, which is good news for fantasy managers who roster him.

 Day’Ron Sharpe tallied 11 points (3-of-4 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Pacers.
 Sunday was a bad day for the Nets, who fell to 0-3 with a blowout loss to the Pacers. Sharpe shot the ball well from the field, but the overall production was underwhelming for a starting center. The promotion certainly raises his fantasy ceiling, but it may take time for Sharpe to deliver the top-100 return some managers hope for. The Nets play three games in Week 2, starting with the Celtics on Tuesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Pascal Siakam recorded 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Nets.
 Siakam has scored at least 23 points in each of Indiana’s first three games, seemingly benefiting from Tyrese Haliburton’s return from a ruptured Achilles tendon. Siakam may not be an elite fantasy option, but his ceiling has been raised considerably after injuries and instability at point guard damaged his value in 2025-26. The Pacers play four games in Week 2, starting with the Bucks on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jay Huff 
 IND

 Jay Huff notched 14 points (5-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Nets.
 The Pacers lost starting center Ivica Zubac to a sprained left ankle in the first quarter of Sunday’s game, giving more minutes to Huff and Obi Toppin (16/6/2 with four three-pointers). While the latter was more productive offensively, Huff blocked three shots and didn’t have a bad offensive game himself. The Pacers play the Bucks on Monday, which could mean Huff gets a spot start. He and Toppin are worth streaming as long as Zubac is out. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
